title: How are you guys making your assets?
author: Fair_Ad_9505
selftext:
Hey yall! New to development. I have little experience with 3d programs. Everything in my map is handsculpted with assets i bought from the store/Frankensteined. But armor and character models require more precision. I'm shooting for that old morrowind look. So meaning hand painted oil textures shooting for realism on low poly models. Alpha masks for anything that's thin. 

I've tried using meshy but all it does is give me fortnite, I've tried using opus 5.5 in blender but all it does is give me runscape. I've seen so many games with cool assets and I just want to know what your secrete is lmao. Obviously if I have to I'll learn the programs myself but it's an ambitious game and it's me and my best friend. And I happen to be the entire art team lmao

comments.author: W3103_
comments.body:
Tripo works very well but I got annoyed at the paid tiers and the ‘free’ option still involved paying for downloads

Literally told Claude code last night to build a 3D asset generator that builds them from 2d images - and it literally one shotted it. The paint work needs manual touching up but still, it’s amazing really

No tripo needed 🤣

replies.author: W3103_
replies.body:
Here's my actual prompt I used, verbatim. I was speaking into the mic so its not a hyper amazing prompt;

So is it possible to make a program that we can use to make our models a bit better? So I'm thinking if we make our own machine that can convert images to 3d models. basically I've found a few tools that can do it, like tripo. So it seems like it's something that we can make. 

I want it so I can upload a picture of for example, a  fish into the machine and it will make the perfect asset of that fish for the game, and then it's just literally a matter of saying to you okay that's done take that file, And then you can ship it to the game, and configure its skeleton and movement. And it communicates with the game development. And basically says, to the main Claude coding session, here's the fish or Whatever it is. 

 Because I think if we build the models on this app instead, it will make them look better and it's less tokens for you, if the app is actually doing it itself every time.  Is that possible to build?

comments.author: No_Entrepreneur6548
comments.body: In order to get better outputs you need to give it better inputs. If you're making a bus, give it a specific bus you're making. Ask it to find real reference shots of those elements. And most important, do not give up at the first prompt. Getting a detailed model out is not a 1 shot, but could be multiple layered prompts that you drive in the right direction. Character models - ask Opus how to make good looking humans in Blender, there is a free blender plugin that has humans already built and rigged so you dont have to do it. Its very important to drive your art style EARLY and realize you'll need to ask for a ton of detail as you go on.

comments.author: Bitwizarding
comments.body:
I've been using Tripo and Meshy and sometimes using Blender myself or having Claude use Blender to do things like cut models in half and mirror them or rig and animate them. 

I wouldn't say I get one look from Tripo or Meshy. It depends more on what image you give it and how many triangles/quads you give it. I've made models with 5 million triangles or with 3000. Some settings are better for organic life forms and other are better for symmetrical game assets.

I feel like the image models have a big difference if you use them. Nano Banana seems more cartoony given the same prompt compared to chatgpt2.5. There are a lot if different settings to play with. Sometimes you need to use multi-view. Sometimes I generate 9 models at once in a 3x3 grid.

comments.author: Disastrous-Gain5870
comments.body: Honestly your best bet is either going low poly and having Claude use code to make them, be wary this will take multiple iterations, or just using free assets. Other than that you could always pay someone or learn how to do it yourself. I just don’t find that any service is up to snuff yet, but I’m sure in 6 months or less they will be.

comments.author: NachoPirateX
comments.body: The Morrowind look is mostly textures, not geometry. AI bakes in clean, smooth textures and that's why you keep getting Fortnite. Try decimating the generated model to around 500 to 2k tris and toss the texture. Then repaint at 256 or 512, project photo textures in Blender, which some dark grime in the crevices.
